name: Ammonites
also_known_as: Zamzummims (the earlier inhabitants of their land)
summary: A kingdom on the upper Jabbok river, centred on Rabbah — today's Amman, capital of Jordan. The Ammonites came from Lot's younger daughter. They fought Israel under Jephthah, Saul and David, and gave Solomon a wife, Naamah, whose son Rehoboam stands in the royal line of Judah and in Jesus' genealogy.
name_meaning: Ben-ammi, 'son of my (paternal) kin' or 'son of my people'.

origin.account: Lot's younger daughter, following her sister, conceived by her father in the cave above Zoar and bore a son named Ben-ammi: 'the same is the father of the children of Ammon unto this day.'

lineage.notes: Brother nation to Moab and a relative of Israel through Lot. God gave the Ammonites their land and forbade Israel to take it: 'I will not give thee of the land of the children of Ammon any possession; because I have given it unto the children of Lot.'

homeland.region: Ammon — the upper Jabbok, east of Gilead
homeland.description: A compact kingdom on the edge of the desert, around the springs of the Jabbok (Nahr az-Zarqa). The Jabbok was 'the border of the children of Ammon'. Rabbah, 'the city of waters', sat on an easily defended hill with a spring below.
homeland.modern_location: The Amman metropolitan area and surrounding Balqa region of Jordan.

places.name: Rabbah (Rabbath of the children of Ammon)
places.note: Royal city. Og's iron bedstead was kept there; Joab besieged it and Uriah the Hittite was killed at its walls. Called Philadelphia in Greek and Roman times.

places.name: River Jabbok
places.note: Ammon's border with Israel; where Jacob wrestled.

places.name: Jabesh-gilead
places.note: The city Nahash besieged, whose rescue made Saul king in fact.

places.name: Tell el-'Umeiri
places.note: Excavated site where the seal naming King Baalis's servant was found.

timeline.event: Ben-ammi born to Lot's younger daughter.
The Ammonites take their land from a giant people they called Zamzummims.
Ammon, with Moab, is barred from the congregation for not meeting Israel with bread and water and for hiring Balaam.
Ammon joins Eglon against Israel, and later oppresses Gilead eighteen years until Jephthah defeats them. The disputed land is argued over by messengers.
Nahash the Ammonite besieges Jabesh-gilead and demands every man's right eye. Saul rescues the city.
Hanun son of Nahash humiliates David's ambassadors; war follows. During the siege of Rabbah David sins with Bathsheba and arranges Uriah's death. Rabbah falls and David takes the crown of their king.
Solomon marries Naamah the Ammonitess and builds a high place for Molech (Milcom).
Ammon invades Judah under Jehoshaphat; Jotham later receives tribute from them. Amos condemns their atrocities in Gilead.
Baalis king of the Ammonites sends Ishmael son of Nethaniah to murder Gedaliah, the governor Babylon set over Judah.
Tobiah 'the servant, the Ammonite' opposes Nehemiah's rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls and is later thrown out of a temple chamber.

religion.practices: Milcom, 'the abomination of the children of Ammon', was the national god. Scripture links Molech worship to passing children through fire, which the law forbade on pain of death. Josiah defiled the high place Solomon had built for Milcom.

importance: Ammon is a constant border pressure in Israel's story — the enemy that set up Jephthah's judgeship, Saul's first victory and the war in which David fell into adultery and murder. The Bible shows ordinary history and moral history running together: Uriah dies at the walls of Rabbah. Ammon is also inside the royal line. Solomon's son and successor Rehoboam was born to Naamah the Ammonitess, so an Ammonite woman is an ancestor of every later king of Judah and appears (through Roboam) in Matthew's genealogy of Christ.

impact.how: The Ammonite war led to Jephthah's rash vow and its tragic cost.
Victory over Nahash confirmed Saul as king before all Israel at Gilgal.
While Joab besieged Rabbah, David stayed home; the siege gave him cover to have Uriah killed.

impact.who: Gedaliah and the remnant of Judah
impact.how: Baalis's plot led to Gedaliah's murder and the flight of the survivors to Egypt.
Tobiah's opposition shaped the rebuilding of the walls — builders worked with a weapon in one hand.

notable_people.name: Nahash
notable_people.role: King who besieged Jabesh-gilead; later showed kindness to David

notable_people.name: Shobi son of Nahash
notable_people.role: Brought food to David at Mahanaim when he fled Absalom

notable_people.name: Naamah the Ammonitess
notable_people.role: Wife of Solomon, mother of King Rehoboam

key_verses.text: And the younger, she also bare a son, and called his name Benammi: the same is the father of the children of Ammon unto this day.

And when thou comest nigh over against the children of Ammon, distress them not, nor meddle with them: for I will not give thee of the land of the children of Ammon any possession; because I have given it unto the children of Lot for a possession.
Then Nahash the Ammonite came up, and encamped against Jabesh-gilead: and all the men of Jabesh said unto Nahash, Make a covenant with us, and we will serve thee.

And Rehoboam the son of Solomon reigned in Judah. Rehoboam was forty and one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city which the LORD did choose out of all the tribes of Israel, to put his name there. And his mother’s name was Naamah an Ammonitess.
And afterward I will bring again the captivity of the children of Ammon, saith the LORD.

fate.summary: Ammon became a vassal of Assyria and then Babylon. Josephus records Nebuchadnezzar's campaign against it about 582 BC. In the Hellenistic age Ptolemy II rebuilt Rabbah as Philadelphia, which became one of the Decapolis cities under Rome. Ammonites are still mentioned in the 2nd century BC (Judas Maccabeus fought them, according to 1 Maccabees 5:6), after which they disappear as a distinct people. Jeremiah promised: 'afterward I will bring again the captivity of the children of Ammon.'

today.summary: The Ammonites no longer exist as a people, but their capital does: Rabbah is Amman, Jordan's capital, whose name still echoes 'Ammon'. On Amman's Citadel hill are Iron Age remains and inscriptions of the Ammonite kingdom.
today.descendants: Absorbed into the Arab and other populations of Jordan over the Hellenistic, Roman and Islamic periods.
today.modern_legacy: The Amman Citadel Inscription, the Tell Siran bottle and royal statues in the Jordan Museum preserve the Ammonite language and kings.

archaeology.name: Baalis seal impression
archaeology.significance: Reads 'belonging to Milkom'or, servant of Baalyasha' — widely identified with Baalis king of the Ammonites in Jeremiah 40:14.

archaeology.name: Amman Citadel Inscription
archaeology.significance: Building inscription in the Ammonite language invoking Milcom.

archaeology.name: Tell Siran Bottle
archaeology.discovered: 1972 at the University of Jordan campus, Amman
archaeology.significance: A small bronze bottle whose complete inscription lists three generations of Ammonite kings, including Amminadab.

archaeology.name: Statue of Yarah-'azar
archaeology.significance: Royal statue with an Ammonite inscription; shows the kingdom's wealth and art.
